name: Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization Migration
description: Migrate virtual machines at scale from legacy virtualization platforms to Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization using the Migration Toolkit for Virtualization.

narratives.name: Migrating Virtual Machines to OpenShift Virtualization at Scale
narratives.description: How organizations migrate VM estates from legacy platforms to OpenShift Virtualization using MTV.

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations operating hundreds to thousands of virtual machines on legacy virtualization platforms face escalating licensing costs, vendor lock-in risk, and the strategic imperative to consolidate onto a Kubernetes-native platform that manages both VMs and containers with unified tooling.

Migrate the entire VM estate from legacy platforms to Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization using the Migration Toolkit for Virtualization, minimizing business disruption through structured assessment, pilot validation, wave-based execution, and automated post-migration verification.

Implement a six-phase migration lifecycle spanning source environment assessment with compatibility analysis and deep inspection, multi-provider connection configuration with VDDK acceleration, network and storage mapping design, migration plan engineering with VM cohort grouping, pipeline execution with cold, warm, and live migration types, and post-migration validation with performance baseline comparison.

Hundreds to thousands of VMs are migrated to OpenShift Virtualization with sustained throughput of 80 VMs per 41 minutes across 8 hosts, achieving enterprise target success rates with migrated workloads validated for boot integrity, network connectivity, storage correctness, and application functionality.

alphas.name: Virtual Machine Workload
alphas.description: Individual VM lifecycle from template creation through production operation and governance.

narratives.name: Migration-Enriched VM Workload Lifecycle
narratives.description: How migrated VMs transform from vendor-specific configurations to Kubernetes-native resources.

narrativeContexts.context: Virtual machine workloads migrated from legacy virtualization platforms to OpenShift Virtualization undergo a transformation from vendor-specific VM configurations to Kubernetes-native VirtualMachine custom resources, with disk formats converted through the virt-v2v pipeline and drivers replaced with VirtIO equivalents.

The migration process preserves the VM's logical identity while transforming its infrastructure binding from source-platform hypervisor APIs to the KubeVirt virtualization stack, with persistent storage shifting from source datastores to Kubernetes PersistentVolumeClaims and networking transitioning to OVN-Kubernetes pod networks.

MTV's validated migration pipeline has demonstrated throughput of 80 VMs in 41 minutes across 8 ESXi hosts and 800 VMs in 57 minutes through multi-plan parallelism, with support for individual disks up to 6TB and programs of up to 5,000 VMs.

The migration-enriched VM workload lifecycle ensures that migrated VMs achieve full operational parity with their source platform configurations, with automated validation confirming boot integrity, network connectivity, storage correctness, and application functionality.

alphas.name: Virtualization Infrastructure
alphas.description: The KubeVirt operator stack and node configuration enabling Kubernetes-native VM hosting on OpenShift.

narratives.name: MTV Operator Stack and Migration Infrastructure
narratives.description: How the MTV operator ecosystem extends KubeVirt for VM migration operations.

narrativeContexts.context: The virtualization infrastructure supporting VM migration extends beyond the base KubeVirt operator stack to include the MTV operator ecosystem comprising the ForkliftController, inventory service, validation service, and migration controller.

MTV operates as a Kubernetes operator deployed alongside the HyperConverged operator, with the ForkliftController CR serving as the primary configuration surface for migration parameters including concurrency limits, VDDK init image references, and transfer network selections.

The MTV operator integrates with the OpenShift monitoring stack through ServiceMonitor resources, exposing migration-specific Prometheus metrics including mtv_plans_status, mtv_migration_duration_seconds, and mtv_workload_migrations_status_total.

A properly configured virtualization infrastructure with the MTV operator stack, adequate transfer network bandwidth, and optimized storage provisioning provides the foundation for achieving enterprise-scale migration throughput.

alphas.name: Migration Readiness
alphas.description: Systematic assessment and compatibility validation of source VMs for migration readiness.

narratives.name: Multi-Layered VM Assessment and Compatibility Analysis
narratives.description: How MTV's multi-layered assessment provides progressively higher confidence in migration readiness.

narrativeContexts.context: Migration readiness assessment transforms an unknown source VM estate into a quantified, risk-scored, compatibility-analyzed inventory that serves as the foundation for all subsequent migration planning decisions.

MTV's multi-layered assessment progresses from metadata-level inventory through validation-service compatibility analysis to deep inspection with guest OS filesystem examination, with each layer providing progressively higher confidence in migration readiness predictions.

The assessment process evaluates VMs against provider-specific compatibility matrices covering seven supported source platforms including VMware vSphere 6.5 through 8.0 Update 3, Red Hat Virtualization, OpenStack, OVA, Microsoft Hyper-V, AWS EC2, and OpenShift Virtualization.

A thorough migration readiness assessment prevents mid-migration failures by identifying and remediating compatibility issues before plan execution, ensuring execution capacity is focused on VMs that will migrate successfully.

alphas.name: Source Provider Configuration
alphas.description: Configuration and management of connections between MTV and source virtualization platforms.

narratives.name: Multi-Provider Connection Management
narratives.description: How MTV manages authenticated access to source VM inventories across seven provider types.

narrativeContexts.context: Source provider configuration establishes the bridge between legacy virtualization platforms and the MTV migration controller, enabling secure authenticated access to source VM inventories and disk data.

MTV implements source platform connectivity through Provider custom resources, each carrying provider-type-specific credential references with seven distinct provider types each requiring unique connection parameters and authentication mechanisms.

Provider health is continuously monitored through Provider CR conditions and Kubernetes events, with the inventory service periodically synchronizing the VM catalog and validating credential freshness to surface connection failures proactively.

Well-configured and validated source provider connections form the essential data path for all migration operations, and their ongoing health directly determines the migration program's ability to discover, assess, plan, and execute VM migrations.

alphas.name: Migration Planning
alphas.description: Network and storage mapping design plus migration plan engineering for VM cohort execution.

narratives.name: Network and Storage Mapping with Plan Engineering
narratives.description: How network and storage translation rules combine with VM grouping to form executable migration plans.

narrativeContexts.context: Migration planning bridges the gap between readiness assessment and pipeline execution by translating the assessed VM population into executable migration plans with precise network and storage mapping rules.

NetworkMap CRs define per-source-network translation rules, StorageMap CRs define per-datastore translation rules, and Plan CRs combine these mappings with VM selections, migration type, and hook configurations into the atomic unit of migration execution with a hard limit of 500 VMs or 500 disks per plan.

Network and storage mappings are reusable across multiple plans enabling standardized translation rules, with PVC name templates using Go template syntax maintaining organizational naming standards and User Defined Networks supported as targets from MTV 2.7.

Thorough mapping design and plan engineering validated through pilot migrations eliminates the majority of execution-time failures by catching configuration mismatches before they affect production migration waves.

narrativeContexts.context: Migration execution encompasses the full operational lifecycle of VM migration from pipeline configuration through pilot validation, production-scale operation, factory automation, and continuous performance optimization.

The migration pipeline supports three strategies (cold with scheduled downtime, warm with CBT-based incremental copy, and live for OpenShift-to-OpenShift), with the controller_max_vm_inflight parameter governing concurrency and pre/post hooks providing Ansible playbook extensibility.

Performance benchmarks establish 10 concurrent VMs per ESXi host as optimal density, while storage copy offload for ten supported vendors typically reduces disk transfer time by 50-80% for large disks.

The progressive maturity from pilot validation through at-scale operations to factory automation represents the core value delivery mechanism, with each stage building on the validated foundation of the previous stage.

activities.name: Assess Source Environment
activities.description: Inventory source VMs, analyze compatibility, and determine migration readiness per workload.

narratives.name: VM Inventory Discovery and Compatibility Classification
narratives.description: How to discover, classify, and assess source VMs for migration readiness using MTV.

narrativeContexts.context: Install the MTV operator, create Provider CRs for each source platform, and use the validation service to classify VMs as ready, conditionally ready, or not ready based on guest OS compatibility, disk format, and provider-specific prerequisites.

Create Provider CRs with platform-specific credentials stored as Kubernetes Secrets, enable inventory synchronization, and review VMs through the MTV console noting resource profiles and configurations. Enable deep inspection for application-aware analysis, then assign VMs to migration cohorts based on application affinity, dependency ordering, criticality tier, and migration strategy.

Common mistakes include failing to validate VMware VDDK version compatibility and NFC memory settings before assessment, overlooking the 47-character VM naming constraint for Kubernetes resources, and attempting to assess the entire VM estate at once rather than progressively by provider type.

activities.name: Configure Source Providers
activities.description: Establish and validate connections between MTV and source virtualization platforms.

narratives.name: Multi-Provider Connection Establishment and Validation
narratives.description: How to configure and validate MTV connections to source virtualization platforms.

narrativeContexts.context: Establish authenticated connections between MTV and each source virtualization platform, with seven provider types each requiring distinct connection parameters, credential formats, and validation procedures.

Gather platform-specific credentials and CA certificates, create Kubernetes Secrets and Provider CRs, then monitor CR status conditions for Ready state. For VMware, build and push the VDDK init image; validate connectivity from worker nodes and test with a non-production VM migration.

Key pitfalls to avoid include using credentials with insufficient permissions that allow inventory sync but fail during disk access, building VDDK init images incompatible with the source vCenter version, and not establishing credential rotation procedures for long-running programs.

activities.name: Create Migration Network Mappings
activities.description: Define NetworkMap CRs translating source VM networks to target OpenShift networks.

narratives.name: Source-to-Target Network Translation Design
narratives.description: How to design NetworkMap CRs translating source networks to OpenShift equivalents.

narrativeContexts.context: Translate source VM network configurations to target OpenShift networking equivalents, mapping each source port group or logical network to either the pod network, a Multus-based secondary network, or explicitly ignored for infrastructure networks replaced by Kubernetes equivalents.

Inventory source networks by function and VLAN assignments, map application networks to Multus-based secondary networks and standard connectivity to the pod network, and configure a dedicated Multus transfer network for at-scale migrations. Create NetworkMap CRs through the MTV console or kubectl and validate through pilot migrations.

Teams frequently encounter issues such as mapping all source networks to the pod network without analyzing VLAN access requirements, neglecting to configure a dedicated transfer network which causes migration traffic to saturate production workloads, and not verifying target NetworkAttachmentDefinitions exist before referencing them.

activities.name: Create Migration Storage Mappings
activities.description: Define StorageMap CRs translating source VM storage to target OpenShift StorageClasses.

narratives.name: Source-to-Target Storage Translation Design
narratives.description: How to design StorageMap CRs translating source storage to target StorageClasses.

narrativeContexts.context: Translate source VM storage configurations to target OpenShift StorageClasses with appropriate access modes and volume modes, ensuring migrated VM disks land on storage with equivalent or better performance characteristics.

Inventory source storage entities by performance tier, select target StorageClasses with Block volume mode for optimal I/O performance, and configure RWX access for VMs requiring post-migration live migration. Configure storage copy offload for supported VMware vendor combinations and PVC name templates using Go template syntax.

Critical risks in this area include selecting Filesystem volume mode instead of Block which causes significant I/O performance degradation, choosing RWO access for VMs needing live migration which requires disruptive re-provisioning later, and not configuring storage copy offload when source and target vendors support it.

narratives.description: How to partition VMs into executable migration plans with appropriate strategies.

narrativeContexts.context: Transform the assessed VM population into executable Plan CRs, partitioning VMs into cohorts respecting the 500-VM/500-disk limit, grouping by application dependency, and assigning cold, warm, or live migration strategies based on downtime tolerance.

Partition VMs by application dependency, source host, priority tier, migration type, and maintenance window. Create plans through the MTV console or API with VM selection, mapping references, hook configurations, and scheduling constraints. Set controller_max_vm_inflight based on cluster capacity, establish execution sequence, and run plan validation.

Practitioners should watch for plans exceeding the 500-VM or 500-disk limit, setting controller_max_vm_inflight too high which causes resource contention that reduces throughput, and not documenting cross-plan dependencies which leads to application connectivity failures when dependent VMs migrate before prerequisites.

activities.name: Execute Migration Plans
activities.description: Run migration plans, monitor per-VM pipeline progress, and manage execution lifecycle.

narratives.name: Five-Stage Pipeline Execution and Lifecycle Management
narratives.description: How to drive VMs through the migration pipeline and manage execution lifecycle.

narrativeContexts.context: Drive VMs through the five-stage pipeline (Initialize, DiskTransfer, ImageConversion, PostHook, VM Creation) by creating Migration CRs, with the controller processing multiple VMs concurrently up to the controller_max_vm_inflight limit.

Initiate execution through the MTV console or kubectl, monitor per-VM pipeline stage progress and Prometheus metrics, manage warm migration cutovers within maintenance windows, and handle failures through per-VM cancel and plan restart operations. Preserve source VMs until application team completes validation.

Frequent errors include starting production plans without completing pilot validation, not monitoring warm migration precopy cycle counts against the 28-snapshot CBT limit, and cancelling entire plans when only individual VMs have failed which loses completed migration progress.

activities.name: Validate Migrated Workloads
activities.description: Verify migrated VM functionality, connectivity, performance, and application health.

narratives.name: Post-Migration Verification and Application Sign-Off
narratives.description: How to validate migrated VMs for functionality, connectivity, and performance parity.

narrativeContexts.context: Validate each migrated VM through a structured sequence confirming boot integrity, network connectivity, storage correctness, application functionality, and performance parity against pre-migration baselines.

Confirm VirtualMachine CR creation with expected resources, verify network connectivity to cluster services and external endpoints, run filesystem integrity checks and database consistency validation, and compare performance metrics against pre-migration baselines. Obtain formal application team sign-off and maintain a soak period before source decommissioning.

Common mistakes include performing only boot verification without validating network connectivity to application dependencies, not comparing post-migration storage performance against pre-migration baselines, and rushing application sign-off without adequate soak time for periodic batch processing discovery.

activities.name: Configure Migration Hooks
activities.description: Develop and attach pre/post-migration Ansible playbooks to migration plans.

narratives.name: Pre/Post-Migration Ansible Playbook Development
narratives.description: How to develop and attach Ansible playbooks extending the MTV migration pipeline.

narrativeContexts.context: Create Ansible playbooks that execute at defined pipeline points (pre-migration before disk transfer, post-migration after VM creation) for source VM preparation, target environment integration, and automated validation.

Implement hooks as containerized Ansible playbooks with idempotent tasks, error handling via rescue blocks, and timeout awareness. Pre-hooks typically stop services and record state; post-hooks register VMs with configuration management, update DNS, and run smoke tests. Each plan supports one pre and one post hook.

Key pitfalls to avoid include writing non-idempotent playbooks that fail on retry after transient errors, embedding credentials in container images instead of mounting Kubernetes Secrets, and implementing long-running validation without timeout guards which blocks the pipeline indefinitely.

activities.name: Optimize Migration Performance
activities.description: Tune concurrency, enable storage offload, and configure transfer optimizations.

narratives.name: Concurrency Tuning and Storage Offload Configuration
narratives.description: How to progressively tune migration throughput from default settings to optimized performance.

narrativeContexts.context: Progressively tune the migration pipeline through concurrency optimization, storage offload enablement, and transfer network isolation to achieve maximum sustainable throughput while maintaining platform stability.

Establish a performance baseline with default settings, then iteratively tune controller_max_vm_inflight targeting 10 VMs per ESXi host, increase NFC memory to 1GB or higher, and configure storage copy offload for supported vendors. Deploy a dedicated Multus transfer network and re-measure after each optimization.

Teams frequently encounter issues such as increasing concurrency without monitoring source host resources which causes NFC memory exhaustion, enabling storage copy offload without end-to-end validation which leads to silent fallback to standard transfer, and not provisioning sufficient transfer network bandwidth for sustained concurrent load.

activities.name: Implement Migration Factory
activities.description: Establish automated migration process combining MTV with Ansible Automation Platform.

narratives.name: AAP Workflow Automation for Continuous Migration
narratives.description: How to build a migration factory combining MTV with Ansible Automation Platform.

narrativeContexts.context: Connect individual migration activities into a continuous automated pipeline through Ansible Automation Platform, transforming migration from a project-based activity into an operational capability with self-service interfaces.

Build four factory components: self-service migration requests through AAP survey forms, automated assessment and planning through MTV API interaction, automated execution and monitoring through workflow templates with status polling, and automated validation and closure with application team notification. Track factory KPIs including cycle time, throughput, and first-pass success rate.

Critical risks in this area include automating the entire lifecycle before establishing reliable manual procedures, building monolithic AAP workflows that are difficult to debug when individual steps fail, and focusing on throughput metrics without tracking quality metrics like first-pass success rate.

activities.name: Define Custom Validation Rules
activities.description: Create OPA/Rego policies for organization-specific pre-migration validation criteria.

narratives.name: OPA/Rego Policy Development for Migration Compliance
narratives.description: How to extend MTV validation with organization-specific OPA/Rego policies.

narrativeContexts.context: Extend MTV built-in compatibility checks with organization-specific OPA/Rego policies addressing naming conventions, labeling requirements, resource thresholds, software compatibility, and migration strategy constraints.

Write Rego policies evaluating structured VM metadata against organizational rules producing pass, warning, or critical results with remediation messages. Create comprehensive test suites covering pass, warning, and critical scenarios, test with OPA CLI, and deploy through ConfigMaps mounted into the validation service pod.

Practitioners should watch for overly strict rules that block legitimate migration candidates without preventing actual failures, not testing boundary conditions such as names exactly at the 47-character limit, and neglecting rule lifecycle management which accumulates obsolete rules for decommissioned source platforms.

activities.name: Troubleshoot Migration Failures
activities.description: Diagnose, remediate, and recover from failed VM migrations using structured procedures.

narratives.name: Six-Step Diagnostic Workflow and Recovery Procedures
narratives.description: How to systematically diagnose and recover from migration failures using MTV diagnostics.

narrativeContexts.context: Follow MTV's six-step troubleshooting workflow progressing from plan-level status through VM pipeline stage identification to pod-level diagnostic detail, with cancel/restart operations for efficient recovery.

Check Migration CR status, review per-VM pipeline stage and error messages, examine conversion pod logs for virt-v2v output, check ForkliftController logs for orchestration issues, validate source provider connectivity, and run must-gather for Red Hat support. Use per-VM cancel to remove individual failures without affecting others, and plan restart to retry.

Frequent errors include skipping the structured workflow and going directly to must-gather collection, not checking conversion pod logs for ImageConversion failures where the most diagnostic detail exists, and cancelling entire plans when only individual VMs have failed.

activities.name: Monitor Migration Progress
activities.description: Track migration metrics, generate reports, and provide visibility into program progress.

narratives.name: Prometheus Metrics and Migration Program Dashboards
narratives.description: How to implement multi-level migration monitoring with MTV Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboards.

narrativeContexts.context: Provide multi-level visibility through MTV Prometheus metrics, custom Grafana dashboards, automated alerting, and regular reporting at daily, weekly, and wave-completion cadences.

Configure MTV metrics scraping via ServiceMonitor resources, create Grafana dashboards for operations and executive views, and configure alerting for critical conditions such as stalled plans and provider failures. Generate daily and weekly reports with trend analysis, timeline projections, and risk assessment.

Common mistakes include not verifying metrics availability after operator installation and discovering gaps during production migration, building dashboards focused on throughput without quality metrics, and setting alert thresholds too aggressively which causes alert fatigue from normal duration variance.

activities.name: Optimize Source Provider Integration
activities.description: Tune provider connections for multi-provider operations and optimize performance.

narratives.name: Multi-Provider Operations and Performance Tuning
narratives.description: How to optimize multi-provider operations and credential lifecycle management.

narrativeContexts.context: Extend initial provider configuration to support concurrent multi-provider operations, credential lifecycle management, inventory synchronization tuning, and per-host transfer optimization for sustained throughput.

Configure multiple Provider CRs simultaneously with independent credentials, establish credential rotation coordinated with source administrators, tune inventory synchronization intervals, and configure multiple ESXi host connections for parallel disk transfer. Implement GitOps management for Provider CRs where security policies permit.

Key pitfalls to avoid include not coordinating credential rotation timing with active migration plans which causes mid-migration failures, failing to increase NFC service memory before high-concurrency waves, and neglecting provider decommissioning procedures after source platform migration completes.

patterns.name: VM Migration Lifecycle
patterns.description: End-to-end coordination of migration from assessment through validation and optimization.

patternViews.name: Design - Assess and Map
patternViews.description: Discover source environment, analyze compatibility, and design mappings.

narrativeContexts.context: The migration team establishes connectivity to source platforms, discovers and catalogs the VM estate with compatibility analysis, designs network and storage translation mappings, and configures the MTV pipeline infrastructure on the target cluster.

patternViews.name: Build - Plan and Pilot
patternViews.description: Create migration plans, configure hooks, and validate through pilots.

narrativeContexts.context: The migration team engineers plans with VM cohort groupings, develops hook playbooks, defines custom OPA validation rules, and executes pilot plans to validate the complete pipeline end-to-end before production-scale execution.

patternViews.name: Run - Execute at Scale
patternViews.description: Execute production migration waves with monitoring and troubleshooting.

narrativeContexts.context: The migration team executes production waves at scale, coordinating warm migration cutovers, diagnosing failures through the structured troubleshooting workflow, validating migrated workloads, and tracking program progress through metrics dashboards.

patternViews.name: Optimize - Scale and Automate
patternViews.description: Optimize throughput, establish factory operations, and finalize the program.

narrativeContexts.context: The migration team optimizes throughput through storage offload and concurrency tuning, establishes the migration factory with AAP for continuous processing, and finalizes the program with comprehensive reporting and source platform decommissioning.

patterns.name: Migration Wave Execution
patterns.description: Repeatable pattern for executing a single migration wave from preparation through review.

patternViews.name: Plan - Wave Preparation
patternViews.description: Final pre-execution checks and stakeholder coordination for the wave.

narrativeContexts.context: The migration team performs final pre-execution checks, validates source provider connections, confirms maintenance windows with application teams, and runs updated validation rules against the wave's VM population.

patternViews.name: Do - Migration Execution
patternViews.description: Execute migration plans, manage concurrency, and handle failures.

narrativeContexts.context: The migration team executes the wave's plans, monitoring per-VM pipeline progress, managing concurrency settings, coordinating warm migration cutovers during maintenance windows, and diagnosing failures through the six-step troubleshooting workflow.

patternViews.name: Check - Validation
patternViews.description: Validate migrated VMs for functionality, connectivity, and performance.

narrativeContexts.context: The migration team validates each migrated VM through the structured sequence, records validation results, obtains application team sign-off, and transitions VM status from migrated to validated in the tracking system.

patternViews.name: Act - Review and Improve
patternViews.description: Review wave results, apply lessons learned, and refine processes.

narrativeContexts.context: The migration team reviews wave results, analyzes failure patterns for systemic prevention, adjusts tuning settings based on measured data, updates the runbook with new solutions, and communicates completion status to stakeholders.
